title: Medibank calls for health reform as it reports $638m full-year profits
full_text:
Medibank has called for long-term health reform to keep the cost of health services down, as cost-of-living pressure forces more Australians into lower-tier policies.
The listed private health insurer reported a 27.5 per cent lift in full-year profits to $638.7m as Australians prioritise health insurance, despite hip-pocket pressure.
Medibank logged revenue of $9.1bn for the 2026 financial year, a 9.2 per cent uptick, with health revenue reaching $8.7bn, 8 per cent higher. Medibank paid out $6.9bn in claims for the 12 months.
The growth in the number of domestic policyholders slowed to 0.6 per cent for its core Medibank service, and 2.4 per cent for its budget-friendly ahm business.
Medibank’s lifted its premiums in April by an average of 5.1 per cent to combat the increasing cost of healthcare.
Medibank chief executive David Koczkar said members would struggle to find relief until more was done at a policy level.
“We’re doing everything we can to keep pressure off premiums,” he said. “More needs to be done at a reform level over the very long term.” Mr Koczkar pointed to an over-reliance on hospitals as a care setting and called on the government to support investment in prevention.
Medibank said members were increasingly opting for cheaper tiers of service, and that aggregators, such as Compare the Market, were increasing their share.
“Cost-of-living pressures have impacted the industry, with policyholder growth skewed to lower product tiers, higher switching and aggregators increasing their share of joins,” it said. It announced a final dividend of 10.9c-per-share, bringing its shareholders’ total distribution to 19.2c-per share, up on the 18c paid out the year prior.
